title: Stochastic Delay Modelling of Streptococcal Transmission: Stability Analysis and Dynamically Consistent Numerical Schemes
headline: Open finding: under Equation (15)’s untruncated Gaussian increments, positivity and invariance of Gamma fail with positive probability.

work.title: Stochastic Delay Modelling of Streptococcal Transmission: Stability Analysis and Dynamically Consistent Numerical Schemes

claims.label: Equation (15) positivity and Theorems 10–11
claims.page: NCBI JATS IDs syb270086-disp-0090, syb270086-mthst-0010, syb270086-mthst-0011 and syb270086-tbl-0001
claims.gist: Equation (15) and Theorems 10–11 claim nonnegative iterates and invariance of Gamma for the stated Gaussian Brownian increments.
claims.statement: For the scheme in Equation (15), Theorem 10 states nonnegativity for nonnegative initial values and Theorem 11 states invariance of Gamma. Under the paper's untruncated Gaussian law, both claims fail as stated.
conditions: Brownian increments are independent N(0,h) variables as stated in the article.
The initial delayed history is nonnegative and satisfies the stated Gamma bound where that theorem applies.
Table 1 parameters include Lambda=mu=0.5, gamma_2=0.08, and sigma_1=0.05.
claims.quantifiers: Theorem 10 asserts positivity for nonnegative initial values and Theorem 11 asserts Gamma invariance for the stated scheme; the counterexamples use admissible constant histories at h=0.01 and, for the stochastic Gamma exit, at h=1.

result.summary: Equation (15) has a Gaussian denominator with positive probability of a negative susceptible update; a boundary history exits Gamma with positive probability.
result.witness: With the constant nonnegative history (S,I,C,A)=(0,0,0,1) and Table 1 values Lambda=mu=0.5, gamma2=0.08, sigma1=0.05, Equation (15) gives S1=0.58h/(1+0.5h-0.05 DeltaB). For every h>0, the Gaussian event DeltaB>(1+0.5h)/0.05 has positive probability and makes S1<0. From the boundary history (1,0,0,0) in Gamma, S1=(1+0.5h)/(1+0.5h-0.05 DeltaB); positive increments below the pole give S1>1=Lambda/mu, so the trajectory leaves Gamma with positive probability (exactly 1/2 at h=1, ignoring the zero-probability pole).
result.argument: A nondegenerate Gaussian increment has unbounded support and assigns positive probability to each nonempty upper tail. The first history therefore produces a negative state with positive probability, contradicting almost-sure positivity. Symmetry gives probability 1/2 of a positive increment at the boundary history, and any such increment before the pole raises S1 above the invariant bound. Arbitrarily small tail probabilities still refute the unqualified pathwise or almost-sure claims.
not_claimed: The finding does not say every simulated path fails.
No modified or truncated-noise scheme is assessed.
The separate near-zero-increment population-bound check is not needed for the Gaussian counterexamples.
result.repair_note: A revised scheme would need bounded noise or updates that enforce positive denominators and the claimed invariant; no repaired theorem is assessed.
